  4014: Void
  4015: [P4520] Annex G (normative):
  4016: Propagation conditions
  4017: [P4522] G.1	Static propagation condition
  4018: [P4523] The propagation for the static performance measurement is an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) environment. No fading or multi-paths exist for this propagation model.
  4019: [P4524] G.2	Multi-path fading propagation conditions
  4020: [P4525] The multipath propagation conditions consist of several parts:
  4021: [P4526] -	A delay profile in the form of a "tapped delay-line", characterized by a number of taps at fixed positions on a sampling grid. The profile can be further characterized by the r.m.s. delay spread and the maximum delay spanned by the taps.
  4022: [P4527] -	A combination of channel model parameters that include the Delay profile and the Doppler spectrum that is characterized by a classical spectrum shape and a maximum Doppler frequency.
  4023: [P4528] -	Different models are used for FR1 (410 MHz - 7.125 GHz) and FR2 (24.25 GHz – 52.6 GHz).
  4024: [P4529] G.2.1	Delay profiles
  4025: [P4530] The delay profiles are simplified from the TR 38.901 [20] TDL models. The simplification steps are shown below for information. These steps are only used when new delay profiles are created. Otherwise, the delay profiles specified in G.2.1.1 can be used as such.
  4026: [P4531] -	Step 1: Use the original TDL model from TR 38.901 [20].
  4027: [P4532] -	Step 2: Re-order the taps in ascending delays
  4028: [P4533] -	Step 3: Perform delay scaling according to the procedure described in clause 7.7.3 in TR 38.901 [20].
  4029: [P4534] -	Step 4: Apply the quantization to the delay resolution 5 ns. This is done simply by rounding the tap delays to the nearest multiple of the delay resolution.
  4030: [P4535] -	Step 5: If multiple taps are rounded to the same delay bin, merge them by calculating their linear power sum.

  2307: [P2458] 7.4	In-band selectivity and blocking
  2308: [P2459] 7.4.1	Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS)
  2309: [P2460] 7.4.1.1	Definition and applicability
  2310: [P2461] Adjacent channel selectivity (ACS) is a measure of the receiver's ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned channel frequency at the antenna connector for BS type 1-C or TAB connector for BS type 1-H in the presence of an adjacent channel signal with a specified centre frequency offset of the interfering signal to the band edge of a victim system.
  2311: [P2462] 7.4.1.2	Minimum requirement
  2312: [P2463] The minimum requirement for BS type 1-C and BS type 1-H are in TS 38.104 [2], clause 7.4.1.2.
  2313: [P2464] 7.4.1.3	Test purpose
  2314: [P2465] The test purpose is to verify the ability of the BS receiver filter to suppress interfering signals in the channels adjacent to the wanted channel.
  2315: [P2466] 7.4.1.4	Method of test
  2316: [P2467] 7.4.1.4.1	Initial conditions
  2317: [P2468] Test environment: Normal; see annex B.2.
  2318: [P2469] RF channels to be tested for single carrier (SC): M; see clause 4.9.1.

  2561: [P2744] 7.8	In-channel selectivity
  2562: [P2745] 7.8.1	Definition and applicability
  2563: [P2746] In-channel selectivity (ICS) is a measure of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned resource block locations at the antenna connector for BS type 1-C or TAB connector for BS type 1-H in the presence of an interfering signal received at a larger power spectral density. In this condition a throughput requirement shall be met for a specified reference measurement channel. The interfering signal shall be an NR signal which is time aligned with the wanted signal.

  2565: [P2748] The minimum requirements for BS type 1-C and BS type 1-H are in TS 38.104 [2], clause 7.8.2.

  2567: [P2750] The purpose of this test is to verify the BS receiver ability to suppress the IQ leakage.

  3756: [P4172] The timing offset base value for PRACH preamble format 0 is set to 50% of Ncs. Then the loop is being reset and the timing offset is set again to 0. The timing offset scheme for PRACH preamble format A1, A2, A3, B4, C0 and C2 is presented in figure 8.4.1.4.2-3.

CONTEXT:
  3215: [P3541] The performance requirement of single user PUCCH format 0 for ACK missed detection is determined by the two parameters: probability of false detection of the ACK and the probability of detection of ACK. The performance is measured by the required SNR at probability of detection equal to 0.99. The probability of false detection of the ACK shall be 0.01 or less.
  3216: [P3542] The probability of false detection of the ACK is defined as a conditional probability of erroneous detection of the ACK when input is only noise.
  3217: [P3543] The probability of detection of ACK is defined as conditional probability of detection of the ACK when the signal is present.
  3218: [P3544] The transient period as specified in TS 38.101-1 [21] clause 6.3.3.1 is not taken into account for performance requirement testing, where the RB hopping is symmetric to the CC center, i.e. intra-slot frequency hopping is enabled.
  3219: [P3545] Which specific test(s) are applicable to BS is based on the test applicability rules defined in clause 8.1.2.
  3220: [P3546] 8.3.1.2	Minimum Requirement
  3221: [P3547] The minimum requirements are in TS 38.104 [2] clause 8.3.1 and 8.3.2.
  3222: [P3548] 8.3.1.3	Test purpose
  3223: [P3549] The test shall verify the receiver's ability to detect ACK under multipath fading propagation conditions for a given SNR.
  3224: [P3550] 8.3.1.4	Method of test

CONTEXT:
  3245: [P3577] The performance requirement of PUCCH format 1 for NACK to ACK detection is determined by the two parameters: probability of false detection of the ACK and the NACK to ACK detection probability. The performance is measured by the required SNR at probability of the NACK to ACK detection equal to 0.1% or less. The probability of false detection of the ACK shall be 0.01 or less.
  3246: [P3578] The probability of false detection of the ACK is defined as a conditional probability of erroneous detection of the ACK at particular bit position when input is only noise. Each false bit detection is counted as one error.
  3247: [P3579] The NACK to ACK detection probability is the probability of detecting an ACK bit when an NACK bit was sent on particular bit position. Each NACK bit erroneously detected as ACK bit is counted as one error. Erroneously detected NACK bits in the definition do not contain the NACK bits which are mapped from DTX, i.e. NACK bits received when DTX is sent should not be considered.
  3248: [P3580] The transient period as specified in TS 38.101-1 [21] clause 6.3.3.1 is not taken into account for performance requirement testing, where the RB hopping is symmetric to the CC center, i.e. intra-slot frequency hopping is enabled.
  3249: [P3581] Which specific test(s) are applicable to BS is based on the test applicability rules defined in clause 8.1.2.

CONTEXT:
  3417: [P3777] 8.3.6.1.1.1	Definition and applicability
  3418: [P3778] The performance requirement of multi-slot PUCCH format 1 for NACK to ACK detection is determined by the two parameters: probability of false detection of the ACK and the NACK to ACK detection probability. The performance is measured by the required SNR at probability of the NACK to ACK detection equal to 0.1 % or less. The probability of false detection of the ACK shall be 1 % or less.
  3419: [P3779] The probability of false detection of the ACK is defined as a conditional probability of erroneous detection of the ACK at particular bit position when input is only noise. Each false bit detection is counted as one error.
  3420: [P3780] The NACK to ACK detection probability is the probability of detecting an ACK bit when an NACK bit was sent on particular bit position. Each NACK bit erroneously detected as ACK bit is counted as one error. Erroneously detected NACK bits in the definition do not contain the NACK bits which are mapped from DTX, i.e. NACK bits received when DTX is sent should not be considered.
  3421: [P3781] Which specific test(s) are applicable to BS is based on the test applicability rules defined in clause 8.1.2.2.
  3422: [P3782] 8.3.6.1.1.2	Minimum Requirement
  3423: [P3783] The minimum requirement is in TS 38.104 [2] clause 8.3.3.
  3424: [P3784] 8.3.6.1.1.3	Test purpose
  3425: [P3785] The test shall verify the receiver's ability not to falsely detect NACK bits as ACK bits under multipath fading propagation conditions for a given SNR.
  3426: [P3786] 8.3.6.1.1.4	Method of test
  3427: [P3787] 8.3.6.1.1.4.1	Initial conditions
  3428: [P3788] Test environment: Normal; see annex B.2.
  3429: [P3789] RF channels to be tested: for single carrier: M; see clause 4.9.1.
  3430: [P3791] 8.3.6.1.1.4.2	Procedure
  3431: [P3792] 1)	Connect the BS tester generating the wanted signal, multipath fading simulators and AWGN generators to all BS antenna connectors for diversity reception via a combining network as shown in annex D.5 and D.6 for BS type 1-C and BS type 1-H respectively.

  3433: [P3794] Table 8.3.6.1.1.4.2-1: AWGN power level at the BS input

  3553: [P3932] Note that the procedure described in this clause for ACK missed detection has the same condition as that described in clause 8.3.8.1.4.2 for NACK to ACK detection. Both statistics are measured in the same testing.

CONTEXT:
  3648: [P4044] 8.3.12.1.1	Definition and applicability
  3649: [P4045] The performance requirement of PUCCH format 1 with DM-RS bundling for NACK to ACK detection is determined by the two parameters: probability of false detection of the ACK and the NACK to ACK detection probability. The performance is measured by the required SNR at probability of the NACK to ACK detection equal to 0.1 % or less. The probability of false detection of the ACK shall be 1 % or less.
  3650: [P4046] The probability of false detection of the ACK is defined as a conditional probability of erroneous detection of the ACK at particular bit position when input is only noise. Each false bit detection is counted as one error.
  3651: [P4047] The NACK to ACK detection probability is the probability of detecting an ACK bit when a NACK bit was sent on particular bit position. Each NACK bit erroneously detected as ACK bit is counted as one error. Erroneously detected NACK bits in the definition do not contain the NACK bits which are mapped from DTX, i.e. NACK bits received when DTX is sent should not be considered.
  3652: [P4048] Which specific test(s) are applicable to BS is based on the test applicability rules defined in clause 8.1.2.10.
  3653: [P4049] 8.3.12.1.2	Minimum Requirement
  3654: [P4050] The minimum requirement is in TS 38.104 [2] clause 8.3.3.
  3655: [P4051] 8.3.12.1.3	Test purpose
  3656: [P4052] The test shall verify the receiver's ability not to falsely detect NACK bits as ACK bits under multipath fading propagation conditions for a given SNR.
  3657: [P4053] 8.3.12.1.4	Method of test
  3658: [P4054] 8.3.12.1.4.1	Initial conditions
  3659: [P4055] Test environment: Normal; see annex B.2.
  3660: [P4056] RF channels to be tested: for single carrier: M; see clause 4.9.1.
  3661: [P4058] 8.3.12.1.4.2	Procedure
  3662: [P4059] 1)	Connect the BS tester generating the wanted signal, multipath fading simulators and AWGN generators to all BS antenna connectors for diversity reception via a combining network as shown in annex D.5 and D.6 for BS type 1-C and BS type 1-H respectively.
  3663: [P4060] 2)	Adjust the AWGN generator, according to the combinations of SCS and channel bandwidth defined in Table 8.3.12.1.4.2-1.

CONTEXT:
  3674: [P4075] 8.3.12.2	ACK missed detection
  3675: [P4076] 8.3.12.2.1	Definition and applicability
  3676: [P4077] The performance requirement of PUCCH format 1 for ACK missed detection is determined by the two parameters: probability of false detection of the ACK and the probability of detection of ACK. The performance is measured by the required SNR at probability of detection equal to 0.99. The probability of false detection of the ACK shall be 0.01 or less.
  3677: [P4078] The probability of false detection of the ACK is defined as a conditional probability of erroneous detection of the ACK when input is only noise.
  3678: [P4079] The probability of detection of ACK is defined as conditional probability of detection of the ACK when the signal is present.
  3679: [P4080] 8.3.12.2.2	Minimum Requirement
  3680: [P4081] The minimum requirement is in TS 38.104 [2] clause 8.3.3.
  3681: [P4082] 8.3.12.2.3	Test purpose
  3682: [P4083] The test shall verify the receiver's ability to detect ACK bits under multipath fading propagation conditions for a given SNR.

  3754: [P4169] 7)	The test signal generator sends a preamble and the receiver tries to detect the preamble. This pattern is repeated as illustrated in figure 8.4.1.4.2-1. The preambles are sent with certain timing offsets as described below. The following statistics are kept: the number of preambles detected in the idle period and the number of missed preambles.
  3755: [P4171] Figure 8.4.1.4.2-1: PRACH preamble test pattern
  3756: [P4172] The timing offset base value for PRACH preamble format 0 is set to 50% of Ncs. This offset is increased within the loop, by adding in each step a value of 0.1us, until the end of the tested range, which is 0.9us. Then the loop is being reset and the timing offset is set again to 50% of Ncs. The timing offset scheme for PRACH preamble format 0 and 1 is presented in figure 8.4.1.4.2-2.
  3757: [P4174] Figure 8.4.1.4.2-2: Timing offset scheme for PRACH preamble format 0 and 1
  3758: [P4175] The timing offset base value for PRACH preamble format A1, A2, A3, B4, C0 and C2 is set to 0. This offset is increased within the loop, by adding in each step a value of 0.1us, until the end of the tested range, which is 0.8 us. Then the loop is being reset and the timing offset is set again to 0. The timing offset scheme for PRACH preamble format A1, A2, A3, B4, C0 and C2 is presented in figure 8.4.1.4.2-3.
  3759: [P4177] Figure 8.4.1.4.2-3: Timing offset scheme for PRACH preamble format A1 A2, A3, B4, C0 and C2

CONTEXT:
  4010: Characteristics of interfering signals
  4011: [P4514] The interfering signal shall be a PUSCH containing data and DMRS symbols. Normal cyclic prefix is used. The data content shall be uncorrelated to the wanted signal and modulated according to clause 6 of TS 38.211 [17]. Mapping of PUSCH modulation to receiver requirement are specified in table E-1.
  4012: [P4515] Table E-1: Modulation of the interfering signal
  4013: [P4518] Annex F (normative):
  4014: Void
  4015: [P4520] Annex G (normative):
  4016: Propagation conditions
  4017: [P4522] G.1	Static propagation condition
  4018: [P4523] The propagation for the static performance measurement is an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) environment. No fading or multi-paths exist for this propagation model.
  4019: [P4524] G.2	Multi-path fading propagation conditions
  4020: [P4525] The multipath propagation conditions consist of several parts:
  4021: [P4526] -	A delay profile in the form of a "tapped delay-line", characterized by a number of taps at fixed positions on a sampling grid. The profile can be further characterized by the r.m.s. delay spread and the maximum delay spanned by the taps.
  4022: [P4527] -	A combination of channel model parameters that include the Delay profile and the Doppler spectrum that is characterized by a classical spectrum shape and a maximum Doppler frequency.
  4023: [P4528] -	Different models are used for FR1 (410 MHz - 7.125 GHz) and FR2 (24.25 GHz – 52.6 GHz).
  4024: [P4529] G.2.1	Delay profiles
  4025: [P4530] The delay profiles are simplified from the TR 38.901 [20] TDL models. The simplification steps are shown below for information. These steps are only used when new delay profiles are created. Otherwise, the delay profiles specified in G.2.1.1 can be used as such.
  4026: [P4531] -	Step 1: Use the original TDL model from TR 38.901 [20].

CONTEXT:
  4011: [P4514] The interfering signal shall be a PUSCH containing data and DMRS symbols. Normal cyclic prefix is used.   4013: [P4518] Annex F (normative):
  4014: Void
  4015: [P4520] Annex G (normative):
  4016: Propagation conditions
  4017: [P4522] G.1	Static propagation condition
  4018: [P4523] The propagation for the static performance measurement is an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) environment. No fading or multi-paths exist for this propagation model.
  4019: [P4524] G.2	Multi-path fading propagation conditions
  4020: [P4525] The multipath propagation conditions consist of several parts:
  4021: [P4526] -	A delay profile in the form of a "tapped delay-line", characterized by a number of taps at fixed positions on a sampling grid. The profile can be further characterized by the r.m.s. delay spread and the maximum delay spanned by the taps.
  4022: [P4527] -	A combination of channel model parameters that include the Delay profile and the Doppler spectrum that is characterized by a classical spectrum shape and a maximum Doppler frequency.
  4023: [P4528] -	Different models are used for FR1 (410 MHz - 7.125 GHz) and FR2 (24.25 GHz – 52.6 GHz).
  4024: [P4529] G.2.1	Delay profiles
  4025: [P4530] The delay profiles are simplified from the TR 38.901 [20] TDL models. The simplification steps are shown below for information. These steps are only used when new delay profiles are created. Otherwise, the delay profiles specified in G.2.1.1 can be used as such.
  4026: [P4531] -	Step 1: Use the original TDL model from TR 38.901 [20].
  4027: [P4532] -	Step 2: Re-order the taps in ascending delays

For 500km/h scenarios, the Doppler shift was derived such that it corresponds to a velocity of around 500km/h for band n3 for the 15kHz SCS and for band n77 for the 30kHz SCS. However, the same Doppler shift requirement shall be applied regardless of the frequency of operation of the base station and thus for lower frequencies, the supported speed is higher.

The PN sequence generator is initialized with a starting seed of "all ones" in the first allocated slot of each frame. The PN sequence is continuous over the slot boundaries.
